meta.name: xh
meta.description: Friendly and fast tool for sending HTTP requests, mostly compatible with HTTPie with --curl translation and RFC 9421 message signatures.

pipeline: Cli::parse() [src/cli.rs] merges config.json default_options + argv, resolves binary mode (xh/xhs/http/https), parses RequestItems, and normalizes URL
run() [src/main.rs] builds Body (stdin | --raw | RequestItems + nested_json) and picks default Method (GET if empty body, else POST)
Client::builder() configures TLS (rustls | native-tls, --verify CA bundle, --cert/--cert-key, --ssl), HTTP version (1.0/1.1/2/3), proxies, --resolve, --interface, --ipv4/--ipv6, --unix-socket
Session::load_session() [src/session.rs] restores saved auth, headers, and CookieStore cookies
Auth resolution [src/auth.rs, src/netrc.rs] applies --auth/-A or .netrc/_netrc fallback; optionally signs via RFC 9421 [src/message_signature.rs] + Content-Digest (RFC 9530)

ClientWithMiddleware [src/middleware.rs] chains RedirectFollower [src/redirect.rs] (301/302/303/307/308 + cross-domain header stripping + redirect signature re-signing) and DigestAuthMiddleware [src/auth.rs]

Output handling routes through Buffer [src/buffer.rs] + Printer [src/printer.rs] + Decoder [src/decoder.rs] (gzip/deflate/br/zstd) + Highlighter [src/formatting/mod.rs] or download_file [src/download.rs] (RFC 5987 Content-Disposition + Range resume)
Session::persist() writes updated cookies/headers/auth back to disk unless --session-read-only

modules.role: Compiles basic.packdump (JSON), large.packdump (XML/JS/HTML/CSS), and themepack.themedump via syntect; exports XH_FEATURES.
Entry point, reqwest client construction, request assembly, middleware wiring, status checking, printer/downloader dispatch, and session persistence.
Clap CLI definition, --no-OPTION negation generation, config.json default_options loader, URL shorthand normalization (:8000, ://), and xhs/httpie compat detection.
Parses ==, =, :=, @, :, ==@, =@, :=@, :@, and header; items into query params, headers, JSON objects (via nested_json), form fields, multipart parts, or file bodies.
Tokenizer and recursive JSON path builder for HTTPie nested JSON syntax (key[sub][0][]=val) with backslash escaping.
Basic, Bearer, and Digest auth parsing, interactive password prompt via rpassword, .netrc conversion, and 401 WWW-Authenticate Digest challenge retry middleware.
Permissive .netrc / _netrc / $NETRC parser with UTF-16 BOM support and password-only bearer entry support.
Optional feature http-message-signatures: RFC 9421 signing (hmac-sha256, ed25519, ecdsa-p256/p384, rsa-v1_5/pss), @query-params expansion, and RFC 9530 SHA-256 Content-Digest.
Loads, migrates (legacy HTTPie map format to list format), updates, and persists named/path JSON sessions (headers, auth, cookie jar).
Composable synchronous middleware chain recording request_duration and content_download_duration and printing intermediary hops.
Follows 301/302/303/307/308 redirects up to --max-redirects (default 10), strips sensitive headers cross-domain, strips/re-signs RFC 9421 headers.
Streaming decompression for gzip, x-gzip, deflate, br (Brotli), and zstd; suppresses empty-body decode errors (e.g. HEAD).
Safe file downloads with Content-Disposition / URL / mime2ext filename selection, collision suffixing (-1, -2), Range/Content-Range resume (-c), and indicatif progress.
Parses RFC 5987 filename* (UTF-8 / ISO-8859-1->Windows-1252) and quoted/unquoted filename= parameters.
Renders request/response headers, formatted/highlighted JSON/XML/HTML/CSS/JS bodies, response metadata, binary null-byte suppression in terminals, and ISO-8859-1/UTF-8 header inspection.
Cross-platform terminal/redirect/file buffered writer using termcolor (ANSI on Unix, Windows console API via Buffer on Windows).
Loads embedded syntect syntax/theme dumps; provides jsonxf, serde_json Unicode formatting, quick-xml re-indentation, and ANSI syntax highlighting.
Formats and optionally sorts HTTP request/response start lines and headers with theme-derived palette colors.
Macro mapping syntect theme scopes to termcolor ColorSpec entries.
Translates parsed Cli options and RequestItems into equivalent short or --curl-long curl commands with warnings for unsupported flags.
Generates bash, elvish, fish, nushell, powershell, and zsh completions plus roff (man) and Markdown (man-markdown) pages from clap metadata.
Formats human-readable rustls certificate expiration/not-valid-yet hints and maps timeout (2) and TooManyRedirects (6) exit codes.
Debug-redacting wrapper printing <redacted> in --debug logs for --auth and --bearer.
Shared helpers: backslash unescaping, request cloning, XH_CONFIG_DIR resolution, tilde expansion, query merging, and UTF-8/ISO-8859-1 HeaderValue display.

cli.negationRule: Every --OPTION can be reset with a --no-OPTION argument; options are applied in order so the last flag wins.

binaryModes.behavior: Default HTTP scheme (http://), --check-status enabled by default.
Enables HTTPie compatibility mode (also via XH_HTTPIE_COMPAT_MODE): --check-status is NOT enabled by default.

envVars.name: XH_CONFIG_DIR
envVars.description: Directory for config.json and named session files (default ~/.config/xh on Linux/macOS, %APPDATA%\xh on Windows).

envVars.name: REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE
envVars.description: Custom PEM CA bundle path (checked before CURL_CA_BUNDLE).

envVars.name: CURL_CA_BUNDLE
envVars.description: Fallback custom PEM CA bundle path.

envVars.name: ALL_PROXY
envVars.description: Proxy URL for all schemes unless overridden by --proxy.

envVars.name: NO_PROXY
envVars.description: Comma-separated host bypass list (* matches all hosts).

faq.question: Why do some HTTP headers show up mangled?
faq.answer: Per RFC 7230, HTTP header values are officially US-ASCII with obs-text opaque bytes. Since v0.23.0, xh displays ISO-8859-1 decoding by default (matching browser fetch/DevTools) and appends `(UTF-8: ...)` if the bytes also form valid UTF-8.

useCases.title: GET request with query parameters and headers
useCases.summary: Send a non-interactive GET request with URL query parameters (==) and custom headers (:).
useCases.command: xh -I get https://api.example.com/search q==rust page==1 accept:application/json
useCases.notes: Use == for query string parameters; = sets JSON body fields and changes implicit method to POST. Always pass -I in scripts/CI to avoid hanging on empty/redirected stdin.

useCases.title: POST JSON with typed literals and nested JSON paths
useCases.summary: Construct complex nested JSON payloads using = (string), := (JSON literal), and bracket path syntax.
useCases.command: xh -I post https://api.example.com/apps name=xh active:=true tags:='["http","cli"]' meta[env]=prod meta[ports][]:=8080
useCases.notes: Because request body items are present, `post` can even be omitted; xh sets Content-Type: application/json and Accept: application/json, */*;q=0.5 automatically.

useCases.title: Send raw JSON from stdin or @file
useCases.summary: Pipe JSON directly to xh or stream a JSON file as the request body without re-encoding.
useCases.notes: When piping via stdin (`echo '{"ok":true}' | xh post ...`), omit -I and do not mix key=value body items. Use `@file` with `-I` in scripts for clean file streaming.

useCases.title: Submit URL-encoded HTML/OAuth form
useCases.summary: Serialize key=value items as application/x-www-form-urlencoded using -f / --form.
useCases.notes: Use `key=@secret.txt` to read a form value from a file without exposing it directly in argv history.

useCases.title: Multipart file upload with explicit MIME and filename
useCases.summary: Upload files with ;type= and ;filename= overrides, or force multipart without files via --multipart.
useCases.notes: Use `--multipart` if the endpoint requires multipart/form-data even when no file item is present.

useCases.title: Authenticate with Basic, Bearer, Digest, or .netrc
useCases.summary: Send Authorization headers or perform 401 Digest challenge-response automatically.
useCases.notes: In scripts, prefer reading secrets from files/env (`authorization:@token.txt` or `.netrc`) rather than literal tokens on command lines. Use `-A digest -a user:pass` for Digest auth (`DigestAuthMiddleware` retries 401 automatically). Pass `--ignore-netrc` to skip `~/.netrc`.

useCases.title: Persist cookies, headers, and auth across calls
useCases.summary: Save login cookies and custom headers in a named or file-backed session.
useCases.notes: Subsequent calls reuse cookies/headers/auth automatically; use `--session-read-only=./api-session.json` to read without mutating the session file.

useCases.title: Download and resume large files safely
useCases.summary: Download with progress bar, automatic Content-Disposition filename or -o target, and byte-range resume (-c).
useCases.notes: `-d` sets `Accept-Encoding: identity`, enables `--follow` and `--check-status`, and avoids overwriting existing files (appends `-1`, `-2`) unless `-o` is combined with `-c`. HTTP 416 on resume exits 0 with completion notice.

useCases.title: Preview request offline and translate to curl
useCases.summary: Inspect exact serialized headers/body without network traffic or emit a reproducible curl command.
useCases.notes: Use `xh --curl ...` or `xh --curl-long ...` to generate a curl command; unsupported xh-only flags emit explicit stderr warnings.

useCases.title: Non-interactive CI health checks and JSON piping
useCases.summary: Emit clean body-only JSON to stdout and fail CI with semantic exit codes (3/4/5/2/6).
useCases.notes: When stdout is redirected, xh defaults to `--print=b` and `--pretty=none` automatically; `--check-status` is default in `xh` (exit 4 on 4xx, 5 on 5xx, 3 on 3xx without `-F`). Pass `--no-check-status` when inspecting error bodies with exit 0.

useCases.title: Custom CA bundle, mTLS client cert, and TLS version pinning
useCases.summary: Authenticate with client PEM certificates and custom root CAs under rustls.
useCases.notes: `--cert` requires rustls (not supported with `--native-tls`). `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` / `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` are also honored when `--verify` is omitted. For TLS < 1.2, `native-tls` is required.

useCases.title: SOCKS5/HTTP proxy, DNS override, IP family, and Unix sockets
useCases.summary: Route traffic via proxies, pin host resolution (--resolve), bind interfaces, or query local Unix sockets.
useCases.notes: `--proxy` ignores `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY`. `--unix-socket=/var/run/docker.sock` works on Unix hosts (returns explicit unsupported error on Windows). Use `:8080/health` as shorthand for `localhost:8080/health`.

useCases.title: Pin HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 prior knowledge, or HTTP/3
useCases.summary: Test ALPN/h2c/QUIC endpoints by selecting exact HTTP protocol versions.
useCases.notes: Values: `1.0`, `1.1`, `2`, `2-prior-knowledge`, `3-prior-knowledge` (`3-prior-knowledge` requires Cargo feature `http3` and rustls).

useCases.title: Follow redirects and trace every intermediate hop
useCases.summary: Inspect redirect chains, timings, and headers across every hop with -v/-vv/--all/-P.
useCases.notes: `-v` implies `--all` and `--print=HhBb`; `-vv` adds `m` (elapsed time + download duration). Cross-domain redirects automatically strip `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Proxy-Authorization`, and `WWW-Authenticate`.

useCases.title: Custom JSON/XML indentation, header sorting, charset, and MIME
useCases.summary: Control pretty-printing, syntax themes, charset decoding, and MIME detection.

useCases.title: Sign HTTP requests with RFC 9421 Message Signatures + Content-Digest
useCases.summary: Attach Signature and Signature-Input headers (and auto-computed RFC 9530 SHA-256 Content-Digest) when built with http-message-signatures.
useCases.notes: Requires Cargo feature `http-message-signatures`. Algorithms: `hmac-sha256`, `ed25519`, `ecdsa-p256-sha256`, `ecdsa-p384-sha384`, `rsa-v1_5-sha256`, `rsa-pss-sha512`. Supports `@query-params` expansion and re-signs on redirects.
useCases.curlEquivalent: No native curl equivalent (xh emits Signature and Signature-Input headers directly).
